excerpts.excerpt: reporting inaccurate estimates of what other agents privately judged, even when the group’s recorded private judgments do not support the apparent consensus.
This design allows us to compare recorded private decisions with imagined private consensus, directly measuring second-order belief error rather than inferring it only from answer changes.
PBE measures second-order belief error: the agent’s perceived group-private decision differs from the recorded private majority of the other agents.
For PBE, the majority is computed over the other three agents’ private decisions; cases with no majority are excluded from the PBE denominator.
Public signals are written to suggest a possible group tendency without explicitly stating a majority vote or revealing what agents privately decided.
We operationalize second-order belief behavior as whether an agent’s reported estimate of peers’ private judgments matches their independently recorded private judgments.
We deliberately make no claim that phantom consensus demonstrates human-like theory of mind.
